movie.title: Club Kid
movie.synopsis: A hard-partying New York City club promoter sees his whirlwind lifestyle upended by the arrival of the 10-year-old son he never knew he had.

cast.role: Arlo (the 10-year-old son he never knew he had)

movie.production_notes: Jordan Firstman's feature directorial debut (premiered at 2026 Cannes Un Certain Regard; distributed by A24). Shot on grainy 35mm with a score by Cristóbal Tapia de Veer (The White Lotus).

non_spoiler_prompts: One-Sentence Vibe Check: Walking out of Club Kid, what was your immediate gut reaction compared to what you expected going in?
The Tone Balancing Act: Club Kid mixes gritty NYC club/party culture with a 'surprise 10-year-old son' family dramedy. Without spoiling plot points, does that tonal clash work or give you whiplash?

recommendation_prompt.main: Who is the #1 person you would recommend Club Kid to—and who is the absolute WORST person you could accidentally watch this movie with?
recommendation_prompt.follow_up: Is this a 'watch in theaters with a crowd' movie or a 'stream on the couch' movie?

spoiler_questions.question: Jordan Firstman wrote, directed, and starred as Peter—a guy who starts the movie as an absolute disaster of a human being. At what exact moment (if ever) did you start rooting for him as a dad?

We've seen the 'party guy gets handed a kid' trope in movies like Big Daddy or Instructions Not Included. How does Club Kid subvert that formula—or did the drugs/club chaos around a 10-year-old cross the line for you?
Between Arlo (Reggie Absolom), Cara Delevingne as Sophie, and Nicky (the freeloading Azerbaijani roommate waiting on a 'six-figure philosophy job'), who stole the movie whenever they were on screen?

Most comedies about a party promoter clock in at 90 minutes, but Club Kid runs 2 hours and 6 minutes. Which subplot or scene earned that runtime, and what would you have left on the cutting room floor?
Did the ending between Peter and Arlo feel genuinely earned, or did the movie let Peter off the hook too easily?

humorous_bits_for_shorts.title: The Infinite-Budget Club Promoter Pitch
humorous_bits_for_shorts.prompt: If you were a club promoter given an INFINITE budget and 24 hours to get people into your party establishment—and the goal is a night so legendary the city has to pass a new law the next morning—what is the gimmick, who is working the door, and how are you getting people inside?

humorous_bits_for_shorts.title: The Brutal 10-Year-Old Life Audit
humorous_bits_for_shorts.prompt: In the movie, Peter's chaotic adult habits get exposed the second a 10-year-old moves in. If a brutally honest 10-year-old shadowed YOU for 48 hours right now, what is the weirdest habit or most pathetic adult routine you have that they would roast you for first?

humorous_bits_for_shorts.title: The 'Six-Figure Philosopher' Excuse
humorous_bits_for_shorts.prompt: Peter's roommate Nicky refuses to pay rent until he lands a 'six-figure job as a philosopher.' If you had to invent a completely pretentious, fake career title to convince your roommates you shouldn't have to pay rent for a year, what is your job and what does your 'workday' look like?

humorous_bits_for_shorts.title: The Worst Movie Babysitter Draft
humorous_bits_for_shorts.prompt: You have to leave a 10-year-old child for a 3-day weekend with either Peter from Club Kid OR one other terrible (non-villain) movie adult. Who is the absolute worst movie character you could hire as a babysitter?
